speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any severe headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light? Also, have you had any recent travel or contact with sick individuals?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of taking haloperidol, I need to rule out Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome; have you experienced any muscle rigidity or excessive sweating? Also, I need to examine your neck for stiffness and check your vital signs.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will check your current temperature and blood pressure to assess for autonomic instability. REQUEST TEST: Serum Creatine Kinase

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly elevated creatine kinase level, combined with fever, rigidity, and altered mentation in the context of haloperidol use, strongly points to Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
